reason: Negates the existing FLOPO value class mucronate, as 'unlobed' negates lobed.
'Demarcated' needs the part it is set off from (alar cells from the other laminal cells, the blade from the sheath): a relation without its second term, like 'contiguous'.
Ill-defined veins, borders and trunks are not clearly visible or delimited, as with the rule for 'indistinct'.
A hyphenated compound of two shape values, read as a continuum between them.

target: new: conjunction of two values (papillose FLOPO:0991059 and spiny PATO_0001365)
reason: Moss cells and teeth bearing spine-like papillae: both values hold at once, so the continuum reading of the compound does not fit.
The direction ('downward', 'to the rachis', 'to the margins') carries the value; 'pointing' alone is no quality and the rest is a relation to another part.

label: semi-hastate
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being flat and having a single approximately triangular basal lobe directed outward on one side of the main axis. NOTE: Sibling of PATO:0104352 hastate, which has two basal lobes.
reason: A recurring botanical shape of stipules, pinnules and leaflets with a lobe on one side only; not a kind of hastate, which needs two lobes.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum: orbicular PATO_0001934 - reniform PATO_0001871) with docs/odp/01-approximate-value.md for 'sub'
reason: A compound of two shape values, the first approximate.

label: cavernous
definition: A structure quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's containing numerous large, irregular cavities. NOTE: Differs from PATO:0002078 hollow (one cavity) and FLOPO:0991203 alveolate (surface pits).
reason: Fruit mesocarps and seeds riddled with cavities; no PATO child of 'structure, cavities' covers many internal cavities.

target: new: coloured marks (spotted PATO_0000333 with the colour green of the spots)
reason: Compound of a pattern value and the colour of the marks; one term per colour would multiply, and 'spotted' alone loses the colour.
Negates the existing PATO quality grooved.

label: pseudoverticillate
definition: A spatial pattern quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being crowded at nearly the same level of an axis so as to appear whorled while being inserted at separate nodes. NOTE: Sibling of PATO:0001951 whorled; not whorled in fact.
reason: A distinct leaf arrangement that floras keep apart from true whorls; mapping it to whorled would be wrong.
Knee-like = geniculate, bent abruptly like a knee, as rule C191.
An attribute name, not a value; the examples carry their own values (distichous, imbricate, alternate).
Ear-like lobes and eared bases = auriculate; PO has only the grass leaf sheath auricle, too narrow for these bearers.
'Filled' needs what fills the part (lanate mass, pulp, inclusions); the filling is the content, as with 'covered'.
Leaf-bearing shoots and branches have leaves, as opposed to naked ones.
A lipped corolla limb is two-lipped; lipped carpels, sutures and nectaries (projecting rims) are left without a rule.
A position within a series of like parts (outer bracts, tepals, bristles), stated on the bearer, as rule C374 'outer tepal'.

synonyms: à plus grande largeur au milieu
reason: States where along the length the part is widest (base, middle, apex), a position on the bearer rather than a shape term; elliptic and oblong both fit.
Edentate = without teeth; on leaf margins it amounts to entire (PATO_0104359), but filaments and ridges need the plain negation.
PATO papillary is defined as resembling a small nipple-like projection, which fits nipple-like fruit apices and stigmas.
A hyphenated compound of two shape values, read as a continuum.
Pilose hairs that are gland-tipped: the existing class for an indumentum with gland-tipped hairs.
The statements report scars left by fallen leaves or petioles; 'scar' is a generic part (rejected as a bearer before) and PO has no leaf scar.
Says the fruit is nearly a drupe, a fruit type that PO models as a class; 'sub' is kept as an approximate cue (docs/odp/01-approximate-value.md).

label: nut-like
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's similarity to the appearance of a nut: hard, dry and more or less globose. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991042 cherry-like; for fruits, PO:0030102 nut fruit is the bearer type.
reason: Used for seeds and tubers as well as fruits, so a resemblance quality, as with cherry-like and leaf-like.

target: new: conjunction of two values (reticulate FLOPO:0991100 and tuberculate FLOPO:0991060)
reason: A surface that is both net-ridged and set with tubercles; both values hold, so the continuum reading of the compound does not fit.
PATO strap-shaped is defined as shaped like a narrow band.
A fragment of 'broadest near/above/below the middle': the position of the widest point, as for 'widest in middle'.
